chunks: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz from Ayub ibn Nuh, and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, and Muhammad ibn Ismail from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah, all of them from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'The woman who is not permissible for her husband until she marries another husband.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'She is the one who is divorced, then reverted to, then divorced, then reverted to, then divorced for the third time, so she is the one who is not permissible for her husband until she marries another husband, and he tastes her honey.'

key_terms.مُرَاجَعَة: Reversion/Reconciliation (taking back the wife during the waiting period)
key_terms.يَذُوقَ عُسَيْلَتَهُ: He tastes her honey (idiom for consummation)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a woman to become permissible again to her first husband after three divorces?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi clarifies the specific condition of 'Tanzil' (or 'Tatbiq') in Shia jurisprudence, where a woman becomes permanently unmarriable to her first husband after three divorces unless she marries another man, consummates that marriage, and then divorces or dies. The phrase 'tastes her honey' indicates consummation of the intermediate marriage. It highlights the scholarly consensus on the necessity of a genuine, consummated marriage (not merely a contractual formality) to restore the original marital bond.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Ja’far Al Razzaz, from Ayoub Bin Nuh, and Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, and Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Sama’at, all of them from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The woman who is not Permission for her husband until she marries another husband’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘She is who is divorced, then reverted to, then divorced, then reverted to, then divorced for the third (divorce), so she is (the one) who is not Permissible for her husband until she marries another husband, and he tastes her honey (sleeps with her)’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Ja‘far al-Razzaz has narrated from Ayyub ibn Nuh and Abu Ali al-Ash‘ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from and Humayd ibn Ziyad from Sama‘ah all from Safwan from ibn Muskan from abu Basir who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a woman who cannot become lawful for her previous husband in marriage without marriage with another man. He (the Imam) said, ‘She is a woman who is divorced and he goes back to her, then divorces her then goes back to her, then divorces for the third time. She becomes unlawful for him in marriage until she marries another man who tastes her honey (goes to bed with her).”’
